newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: No sign of peace talks progress in Congo Republic.
newsitem.headline: No sign of peace talks progress in Congo Republic.

text.p: The Congo Republic capital Brazzaville awoke to a second day of relative quiet on Tuesday but there was no immediate sign of progress in efforts to bring the warring parties together for peace talks.

A spokesman for former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, the opponent of President Pascal Lissouba in the conflict, suggested on Monday that there could be no peace talks without a signed agreement on a ceasefire.

"There is no signed agreement on a ceasefire -- there were only statements of intent on both sides," Francois Iboovi said, one day after national mediators led by Brazzaville Mayor Bernard Kolelas urged the two sides to attend Wednesday peace talks.
"It's difficult to talk about peace talks without such an agreement," Iboovi told Reuters.
Lissouba's spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.

Clashes broke out on June 5 when the army surrounded Sassou's home as part of a crackdown on private militias ahead of a now-derailed presidential election planned for July 27. Lissouba, Sassou and Kolelas had all been due to stand.
Kolelas's own supporters were at the heart of similar political and ethnic clashes which killed at least 2,000 people after a disputed 1993 parliamentary election.

The conflict and indiscriminate shelling and rocket fire have forced tens of thousands of people to flee their homes and devastated parts of the former French colony's capital but residents noted a significant lull in shooting.
On Monday evening the odd burst rang out but the last heavy outbreak of shellfire was on Sunday morning.
"It's been particularly calm," said one resident.
Sources close to the mediation process say that the real issue is who should govern when Lissouba's mandate expires at the end of August.
Lissouba says the constitution provides for his mandate to be prolonged for 90 days until elections. Sassou says the constitution envisages a neutral transitional authority governing until elections.
